background: Vanquis Banking Group is a UK specialist lender to customers underserved by mainstream banks, funded by retail savings and lending through credit cards, vehicle finance under Moneybarn and personal loans.
synthesis: Only one of the three main agencies rates the group, at BB- and below investment grade, on a positive outlook, the last move a one-notch downgrade on 7 Aug 2024. The headline capital ratios still look adequate against UK small banks, CET1 of 15.6% below the peer median and leverage of 10.7% in the top quarter, but the run of them is the point: since 30 Jun 2024 CET1 has fallen 4.2 points and leverage 4.7 points. Liquidity has been drawn down on the same scale, LCR of 280% below the peer median after a fall of 806 points and NSFR of 143% also below it though broadly flat (figures to 30 Jun 2026) — a balance sheet that has spent a very large surplus in two years. Turnover at the top of the firm, flagged on 12 Sep 2026, leaves the turnaround without its author; this is the weakest credit in the UK set and deposits here warrant a limit sized accordingly.
